candidates.requestedTitle: Butyrate improves insulin sensitivity and increases energy expenditure in mice
candidates.limitations: Mouse effects do not establish efficacy, dosing or durability in people.

candidates.requestedTitle: Gut microbial metabolites limit the frequency of autoimmune T cells and protect against type 1 diabetes
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: Autoimmune T cells and diabetes development
candidates.limitations: Protection in a mouse model is not prevention or treatment of human type 1 diabetes.

candidates.requestedTitle: Human gut microbes impact host serum metabolome and insulin sensitivity
candidates.designAnnotation: human observational metabolomics with preclinical mechanistic follow-up
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: Microbial branched-chain amino acid metabolism and insulin resistance
candidates.limitations: Human association and experimental model findings require separate interpretation; reverse causation and diet remain concerns.

candidates.requestedTitle: A metagenome-wide association study of gut microbiota in type 2 diabetes
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: Microbiome features associated with type 2 diabetes
candidates.limitations: Case-control association does not establish causality, metabolite exposure or a therapeutic effect.

candidates.requestedTitle: Disentangling type 2 diabetes and metformin treatment signatures in the human gut microbiota
candidates.designAnnotation: human observational analysis of disease and medication signatures
candidates.limitations: Medication exposure must be separated from disease effects; this does not establish treatment mediation.

candidates.requestedTitle: Gut bacteria selectively promoted by dietary fibers alleviate type 2 diabetes
candidates.designAnnotation: human dietary intervention with microbiome analyses
candidates.limitations: A multi-component diet intervention cannot isolate butyrate as the cause; treatment and dietary context matter.

candidates.requestedTitle: Microbially Produced Imidazole Propionate Impairs Insulin Signaling through mTORC1
candidates.designAnnotation: human metabolite observations and experimental mechanistic models
candidates.limitations: Mechanistic models and human associations are different evidence layers; human exposure and mediation need evaluation.

candidates.requestedTitle: Obesity is associated with macrophage accumulation in adipose tissue
candidates.limitations: Adipose and intestinal macrophages are not interchangeable; association alone is not causal proof.

candidates.requestedTitle: Adipose expression of tumor necrosis factor-alpha: direct role in obesity-linked insulin resistance
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: TNF and insulin resistance in obesity models
candidates.limitations: Preclinical intervention does not establish a human anti-TNF diabetes treatment.

candidates.requestedTitle: The NLRP3 inflammasome instigates obesity-induced inflammation and insulin resistance
candidates.designAnnotation: preclinical metabolic-inflammation experiments with human context
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: NLRP3, metabolic inflammation and insulin resistance
candidates.limitations: Species, tissues, obesity state and intervention context require verification before translation.

candidates.requestedTitle: Metabolic endotoxemia initiates obesity and insulin resistance
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: Endotoxin exposure, inflammation and insulin resistance
candidates.limitations: Experimental endotoxin exposure does not demonstrate that an individual has gut-derived inflammation.

candidates.requestedTitle: The human gut microbiome in early-onset type 1 diabetes from the TEDDY study
candidates.outcomeAnnotation: Microbiome features and early-onset type 1 diabetes
candidates.limitations: Observational childhood microbiome patterns do not prove that a metabolite prevents autoimmunity.
